steps.title: Explore AWS CLI
steps.description: Get familiar with the AWS CLI and check your configuration.

verification.command: aws __ran s3.ls && aws __ran sts.get-caller-identity && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Create an S3 Bucket
steps.description: Create a storage bucket and upload files to it.
tasks: Create a bucket: `aws s3 mb s3://opsacademy-lab-$(date +%s)`
Find the name your bucket was given: `aws s3 ls`
Create a test file: `echo 'Hello Cloud!' > hello.txt`
Upload it, using your own bucket's name: `aws s3 cp hello.txt s3://your-bucket-name/`

verification.command: aws s3 ls 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}' | grep '^opsacademy' | while read b; do aws s3 ls "s3://$b/"; done 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'hello.txt' && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: IAM Policy Analysis
tasks: View your policies: `aws iam list-attached-user-policies --user-name $(aws sts get-caller-identity --query 'Arn' --output text | cut -d'/' -f2)`
Read what a policy allows: `aws iam get-policy-version --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FullAccess --version-id v1` (then do the same for your other policy)
Write one line per policy, saying what it allows, into `~/iam-notes.txt`, for example: `echo 'AmazonS3FullAccess: every S3 action on every bucket' >> ~/iam-notes.txt`

verification.command: aws __ran iam.list-users && aws __ran iam.list-attached-user-policies && test -s /home/student/iam-notes.txt && echo PASS || echo FAIL
